reasoning_levels.about: Each model's reasoning levels as its provider's documentation lists them, lowest first, with its default and top level; shown on the model pages.

method_records.about: Numbers the method and limits sections state that neither results.json nor answers.json holds. Each group names where it was recorded; build_page.py checks the key review against results.json's excluded questions.

extraction.source: the extraction and repair log of question set version 2

recalibration_v1.source: the separate cross-validated temperature refit of Open-Jev on question set version 1

exam_check.source: the check on the June 2026 TYT exam's Turkish questions (kept private; only the scores are recorded): exam runs 1 to 14, each with the settings of the setup's run on the book; october holds the five setups added in October and checked this way (runs 10 to 14)

copy_check.source: the check that replaced the correct option's text with a copy of a wrong option, on all 2,198 questions: GPT-6 Astra (run 56); in October d1-ultra (run 208), Jev 1.14 (run 207), Decider v1.2 (run 222), Decider Flash v1.2 (run 228) and GLiDE v1.2 (run 249), the last three on our hardware. original and copy count picks of the original letter and of the copy; the benchmark report's 'Correct option replaced' table holds every count

api.cost_basis: Estimated from published prices and recorded token usage

subscription.cost_basis: Subscription run priced as if we had used the API

free.cost_basis: Free tier used; estimated at the list price for the same model

local.cost_basis: No dollar estimate; see hardware and time

first_cost_marks.about: A saving whose first model ran on our own hardware, by how its cost was counted: 'local' (no maker's price; the cost is left out) and 'maker' (the maker's list price for the same model). The marker after the saving, its tooltip, and the note under the table (shown after the marker, and only when the marker is in the table). The 'maker' marker also follows such a model's own cost.

local.tip: Leaves out the first model’s hardware cost, which we have not estimated.
local.note: Leaves out the first model’s hardware cost, which we have not estimated.

maker.tip: Counts the first model at its maker’s list price for the same model; our hardware cost is not measured.
maker.note: Counts the first model at its maker’s list price for the same model; our hardware cost is not measured.

rank_scale.about: The colours of a decision model's bar in the single-series charts of the Hallucination, Page images and Artificial Analysis pages, from the worst decision model on the chart to the best: dark blue, turquoise, green, yellow. The Topics heat map and the link preview use the same colours. The home page's charts, English reading and English and Turkish colour each setup by its model family (model_families).

model_families.about: Each setup's model family, whose colour its bar or dot takes in the charts of the home page (Turkish reading and grammar, every model group), English reading and English and Turkish: a maker's line of models shares one colour, in every chart and in both model groups. A run belongs to its family by provider and, where one provider serves several families, by model; the build stops unless every run belongs to exactly one. The colours are spread so that families next to each other in the rankings differ.

not_run.reason: Not run: SubQ's API returns its probabilities in 32-bit precision, so their sums miss our 7-decimal check. An allowance for that was approved on 5 November 2026 for its English runs; a Turkish run with “Bilmiyorum” was not part of that request.

structural_check.about: runner/translate_reading.py check on the final translations: the questions with a problem (a missing translation, the option letters, an empty text or the underline markup) and the number of warnings (numbering, numbers, Turkish letters, length). The build stops unless every problem question is flagged.

aa_decision_index.about: Artificial Analysis's Decision Index v1.0 as its post of 22 October 2026 lists it: its models in its order, each with our Text tab setup by run id (null: not in our benchmark). sitebuild/aa_index.py builds aa-decision-index/ from it.

thread.note: Artificial Analysis does not name its GLiDE version. The rest of this page uses Fastino's hosted GLiDE; the cards show GLiDE v1.2, which we ran on our GPU.
